clue.text: Four-and-twenty blackbirds in sour cream! F-word recipe?

indicators.note: a recipe tells you how to mix ingredients, so these letters are to be mixed up and remade

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme pie of blackbirds gets a modern, sweary cookery twist with sour cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' signals that the letters of SOUR CREAM and F-WORD are mixed together. 'Four-and-twenty blackbirds' comes from the rhyme 'Sing a Song of Sixpence', baked in a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of crows (blackbirds in the loose sense) has the traditional collective noun used for twenty-four such birds.

clue.text: Men: those who give nothing away receive violent end

indicators.note: the misers take in a letter, so it goes inside them

parts.note: misers hoard their money and give nothing away

indicators.note: the end of the word violent is its final letter

explanation.surface: Stingy people are told they will meet a violent death.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: misters are men, the title used as a common noun for males.

clue.text: Restore state of sapper on location of shooting

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, RE
a film is shot on a set

explanation.surface: A military engineer's condition is assessed at a film location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns but means filming, the puzzle's running joke; a film is shot on a SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reset a device is to restore it to an earlier state.

clue.text: Entrance hall rent collected, a pound off

indicators.note: the letters of hall rent are gathered up and rearranged once the named letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Rent for a hall is gathered, minus a pound, at the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes one L from HALLRENT, leaving HALRENT, which 'collected' rearranges. 'Entrance' looks like a doorway but is the verb, to charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to entrance someone is to captivate or hold them spellbound.

clue.text: Puzzle is Boatman's tale: love lost, embracing life at last

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, so his own is my

indicators.note: the shortened story wraps round a letter
the zero letter for love is dropped from the story

parts.note: a tale is a story
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the last letter of the word life

explanation.surface: The setter introduces his own story, a lovelorn tale with a twist at the end of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes O from STORY, leaving STRY; 'embracing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mystery is something puzzling or unexplained; also the genre of the theme.

clue.text: Yard is led astray and gives up

indicators.note: going astray means wandering out of place, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard is misled and surrenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges IS LED to IELDS. 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, but it is just Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to yield is to give up or surrender; both take a third-person -s.

clue.text: Boatman's cover is partial, unsurprisingly

indicators.note: something done surprisingly turns out unexpectedly, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: The setter's protective sheet only partly covers things, as one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'un' at the start of 'unsurprisingly' is part of the fodder: PARTIAL plus UN, rearranged by 'surprisingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a waterproof sheet used as cover on boats; a tar is also an old word for a sailor.

clue.text: Beast firm on sitting under overturned vehicle

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come below the reversed vehicle in the down entry
turned over, so the word for a vehicle reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An animal and a business are trapped beneath an upturned car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns CAR into RAC; CO and ON go below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the raccoon is a North American animal, a beast in the general sense.

clue.text: Drama at no stage gives way over police search among some trees

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a street is a way or road

indicators.note: the police word goes inside the bit of trees

parts.note: just part of the word trees, its first three letters
the heat is slang for the police, here hunting someone down

explanation.surface: Drama happens nowhere when the road gives way as police comb the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'police search' leans on slang: the heat are the police, out hunting. 'at no stage' looks like 'never' but literally means without a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Street theatre is performed outdoors, with no stage, so it is drama at no stage at all.

clue.text: Lover's letters leave us emphatically with value and purpose

indicators.note: the letters of the lover are taken away from the longer word, leaving the rest

parts.note: ourselves is the emphatic form of us
the letters making up the word lover

explanation.surface: Love letters part from us with meaning and value.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L, O, V, E and R out of OURSELVES and USES is left. As in 'it has its uses', the plural noun covers both value and purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: uses are the worth and functions of a thing, as in the phrase about having its uses.

clue.text: Eponymous songbird suffered distress

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
to suffer, in the old sense, is to let or allow
to rack is to torment or distress

explanation.surface: A songbird after which something is named was in torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' is the old sense, allowed, as in 'suffer the little children'.
explanation.definitionFit: A title track is the song sharing its album's name, so it is eponymous; the Morse theme music is the theme here.

clue.text: He killed off a detective — not at all sinister

definitions.meaning: Colin ..., author of the Morse novels, had his detective die in the last book
in heraldry the right-hand side, opposite the sinister left

explanation.surface: An author ended his detective's life, though he meant no evil by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' looks like wickedness but is the heraldic left, whose opposite is the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic word for right-hand, the opposite of sinister; and Colin Dexter wrote Morse's death.

clue.text: Detective's first to remove uniform in US venture

indicators.note: the letter for uniform is taken out

parts.note: Morse's first name was Endeavour
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A detective's first step is to take off his uniform for an American project.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse's first name is revealed in the books; dropping a U gives the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an endeavor, in American spelling, is an attempt or venture.

clue.text: Swing, dead after coil set round sergeant's head

indicators.note: the piece for dead comes after the rest
the rearranged coil goes round a letter
letters that are set are arranged anew
the head of the word sergeant is its first letter

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A hanged man swings, dead, after the coiled rope was set round the sergeant's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges COIL to OCIL; 'round' puts S inside it to make OSCIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to oscillate is to swing back and forth.

clue.text: Detective uses bug to catch copper with gold

indicators.note: the insect holds a coin inside it

parts.note: a bug is an insect
a penny is a copper coin, P
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A detective uses a listening device to trap a policeman with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' and 'copper' look like police words, a hidden mic and an officer, but are an INSECT and a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an inspector is a police rank, as Morse was a Detective Chief Inspector.

clue.text: Clash with faction leads to an end to shooting

parts.note: a clan is a faction or group

indicators.note: the last letter of the word shooting

explanation.surface: A clash between factions leads to the shooting stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a clang is a loud clash of metal.

clue.text: Detective left out of scrap

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out

parts.note: a morsel is a scrap of food

explanation.surface: A detective is excluded from a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight but means a small bit, a MORSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Inspector Morse is the fictional Oxford detective at the centre of the theme.

clue.text: See 1
Give a wide berth, taking a berth with a fish

indicators.note: the word for avoid takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to shun is to avoid, to give a wide berth
a bunk is a sleeping berth
a is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Avoid sharing a cabin with a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'berth' has two senses: giving a wide berth is avoiding; a berth is a bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the shubunkin is a variety of goldfish with calico markings.

clue.text: Backstage sound effect for killing casually

definitions.meaning: a thump heard off stage, made by the crew
slang for to kill, the gerund naming the act in a casual way

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a bump heard off stage; the second is the slang verb for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang idiom: to bump someone off is to murder them, and a bump off stage is a noise heard from the wings.

clue.text: Starting crisis in denial upset bankers' host

indicators.note: upset means overturned and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
the start of the word crisis is its first letter

explanation.surface: The start of a crisis is upset by denial among those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2008 crisis saw Icelandic banks collapse, hence 'bankers' host'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland hosted the banks that failed spectacularly in the 2008 financial crisis.

clue.text: Carried on with detectives in bad taste

parts.note: ran means carried on or ran a business
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detectives

explanation.surface: Carrying on with the police detectives showed poor judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad taste' suggests vulgarity but means literal sourness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food has gone off and tastes foul, so it is literally bad-tasting.

clue.text: Plans a scam involving the forgery

indicators.note: a forgery is something faked or made over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Plans for a con trick involving forged documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgery' rearranges A SCAM with THE; 'involving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: schemata are outlines or plans, the plural of schema.

clue.text: Got together with everyone in the club

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside

parts.note: people who got together met
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone met up at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society but is a wooden hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mallet is a hammer-headed club, as used in croquet.

clue.text: Exceptionally wise novice first to make sergeant

indicators.note: the learner letter comes first

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner's car

indicators.note: something done exceptionally departs from the usual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually wise beginner is first to become a sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' rearranges WISE to EWIS, with L put first. Sergeant Lewis was Morse's sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Robbie Lewis is the sergeant who works alongside Morse.

clue.text: Location of shooting craps etc: no moral outrage?

indicators.note: an outrage is a disordered state, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambling den where dice are thrown and morals go out of the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting craps' is a dice game; the anagram of ETC NO MORAL gives its famous casino town.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo, in Monaco, is famous for its casino where craps is played.

clue.text: War is wrong; peace begins with an end to shooting

indicators.note: something that is wrong is out of order, so the letters change places
the beginning of the word peace is its first letter

explanation.surface: War is wrong, so peace begins once the shooting stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' is filming again, not gunfire: 'it's a wrap' is called when a film shoot ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Film jargon: a wrap is the end of filming, called when a shoot is complete.

clue.text: How to sit on bike: quick spin uses no force

indicators.note: the letter for force is not used

parts.note: fast means quick
F is the abbreviation for force in physics
a spin is a short ride

explanation.surface: A quick bike ride needs no effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' means a short trip, a RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits astride a bike, one leg on each side.

clue.text: Trap for attacker in fields of lost middle England

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray, rearranged once one is dropped
the middle letter of the seven-letter word England

explanation.surface: Defenders in the English shires trap forwards who have lost their way.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop L (the middle of ENGLAND) from FIELDS OF and rearrange. In football an offside trap catches attackers.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, the offside rule is the trap defenders spring to catch an attacking player.
